profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC2 sits at 44621 Waxpool Road, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus, which the company's own current campus page places directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing the site as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available; this is a campus-wide total that CloudHQ does not break out by individual building, so it is not applied to this specific building's own capacity figure, and no third-party aggregator figure specific to LC2 was found either. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore, and states a company-wide net-zero emissions target by 2040, along with generator fuel supplied by HVO biodiesel "wherever it is reliably available." CloudHQ markets a "campus within a campus" concept at LC, allowing customers to take multiple LC-numbered buildings as one contiguous deployment. CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record, though this is not independently confirmed for CloudHQ specifically.

Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators, including Amazon Web Services, Digital Realty, NTT, Vantage, and Centersquare/Csquare facilities, within a few miles of CloudHQ's LC Campus. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide, and trade press has separately reported CloudHQ planning a 4-million-square-foot expansion campus in Ashburn beyond the LC Campus's existing footprint.
profile.capacity_note: not published by the operator at the building level. Per CloudHQs own current page for the LC Campus (tier-1 operator source, https://cloudhq.com/campus/lc-campus/), this campus is in the heart of Ashburn, Virginia, directly off Loudoun County Parkway, and totals about 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 MW of total critical IT load across fourteen data centers, with 756 MW available critical load, as of this sessions retrieval. Because this is a fourteen-building campus total, it is not applied to any individual rows critical_it_mw.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CloudHQ, the data center operator, was established in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, per the operators own current about page (cloudhq.com/about/) fetched fresh this session. Fateh previously served as CEO and co-founder of DuPont Fabros Technology, a data center company that sold for 7.8 billion dollars in 2017, and has built and operated more than 700 MW of data center capacity across his career, per CloudHQs own founder page (cloudhq.com/learn-about-our-founder/), also fetched fresh this session. CloudHQ operates as part of the Fateh Family Office, alongside affiliated companies CloudCapital, WindHQ, and Dalian Development, per the operators own about page. The company maintains three regional headquarters, a global headquarters in Washington DC, an EMEA headquarters in London, and an APAC headquarters in Singapore. Per the operators own current about page, CloudHQ now describes 23 global campuses, more than 1,380 MW of contracted critical IT load with more than 6,000 MW of expansion potential, more than 30 million square feet of global data center portfolio, and more than 330 employees. A prior research pass on these rows had already flagged that the domain cloudhq.net resolves to an unrelated Google Workspace and Gmail backup software company, not this data center operator, and correctly redirected to cloudhq.com. This session found a second, separate name collision worth flagging for a future researcher: the Wikipedia article at en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CloudHQ describes yet another different, unrelated company, a cloud data synchronization tool for Google Workspace founded in 2011 by Senad Dizdar and based in San Francisco, not this Ashburn and Manassas Virginia data center operator founded by Hossein Fateh. That Wikipedia article was checked this session and found not to apply, so it is not used or cited as a source here, and no Wikipedia sourced company history is included in this reading. A prior research pass on this row found a single aggregator, DataCenterMap, giving an address of 44621 Waxpool Rd, but flagged this as a likely data quality issue because this rows own OSM coordinates sit roughly 200 meters from the registrys LC1, LC3, and LC4 rows, which that prior pass believed were all on or near Loudoun County Parkway, not Waxpool Road. This session found new corroborating evidence that updates that assessment rather than deleting it: datacenterHawks own dedicated LC2 listing independently gives the identical 44621 Waxpool Road, a second agreeing source, and this registrys LC3 row, also in this immediate cluster, independently carries its own two source agreeing Waxpool Road address, 44631, only ten digits away. Two aggregators agreeing on this exact number, plus a directly neighboring row in the same registry independently landing on the same street ten digits off, together outweigh the earlier single source proximity concern, so the Waxpool Road address is applied here, with the prior sessions original caution preserved in this note rather than removed.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC2 is one building in a fourteen-building LC Campus that totals 1,256 MW of critical IT load with 756 MW still available, located in Ashburn on Waxpool Road. The operator has not published a figure for this building alone, so its individual capacity cannot be stated. Across Virginia, 23 facilities publish power specifications totaling 1,375 MW; this campus alone represents most of the state's disclosed capacity.

The LC Campus sits in the core of Northern Virginia's data center cluster, where power and fiber density support AI workloads at scale. At common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the campus's 756 MW of available capacity could support roughly 19,000 additional racks, an assumption stated for arithmetic only. The operator does not publish which certifications qualify this building or campus to host specific workload classes.

Ashburn has 326 mapped data center facilities of which only 23 publish capacity figures. The LC Campus ranks 24th by published megawatts in Virginia alone, a position that understates its significance because most facilities in the state publish no figure at all. The grid constraints that bind AI scaling to power availability and building footprint run through this cluster with particular force.
